posts.raw_content:
🇺🇸 IF AMERICA IS GOING TO BUILD DATA CENTERS, LET’S DO IT THE RIGHT WAY.

I’m not against data centers. I’m against data centers becoming a burden on American communities while private companies collect the benefits.

If we are going to build them, there should be one simple rule:

NO NET COMMUNITY BURDEN.

A data center should make the community BETTER OFF — not worse off.

🔒 PRIVACY MUST BE OPT-IN — NOT OPT-OUT

Americans should own their personal data.

No company should be allowed to collect, sell, analyze, or share personal information beyond what is absolutely necessary to provide a service unless the individual AFFIRMATIVELY OPTS IN.

And enough with clicking through privacy notices on every website.

Give Americans a ONE-TIME NATIONAL PRIVACY SETTING through their phone, computer, or browser.

Choose your privacy level once.

Websites and companies must honor it automatically.

No endless pop-ups.
No deceptive “Accept All” buttons.
No dark patterns.
No “by continuing to browse, you agree.”

Your privacy should be the DEFAULT — not something you have to fight for.

⚡ DATA CENTERS PAY 100% OF THEIR POWER COSTS

If a data center requires new power plants, transmission lines, substations, grid upgrades or additional capacity, THE DATA CENTER PAYS FOR IT.

Not homeowners.
Not small businesses.
Not local taxpayers.
Not through hidden increases in everyone's electric bills.

And if a data center receives a special power arrangement or discounted electricity, the surrounding community should receive a substantial discount as well.

💧 WATER MUST BE RECYCLED

Data centers should use closed-loop cooling and advanced filtration and recycling systems whenever technologically feasible.

Water should be:

USED → FILTERED → TREATED → REUSED

—not continuously taken from a community’s drinking-water supply and discharged as wastewater.

And here is a critical rule:

IF RESIDENTS ARE REQUIRED TO CONSERVE WATER, DATA CENTERS MUST CONSERVE WATER TOO.

If residents face mandatory water restrictions during a drought, data centers face the same restrictions — or stricter ones.

If residents lose water service, a data center does NOT get priority access to the remaining municipal water supply.

⚡ THE SAME RULE MUST APPLY TO ELECTRICITY AND OTHER ESSENTIAL RESOURCES.

If residents are required to reduce electricity consumption during a grid emergency, data centers must reduce their consumption too.

If residents are subjected to rolling blackouts, data centers should not receive preferential treatment simply because they are large commercial customers.

Residents’ essential needs come FIRST.

NO PREFERENTIAL ACCESS.

No special contracts.
No sweetheart agreements.
No backroom exemptions.
No “we’re too important to shut down.”

🏗️ DATA CENTERS PAY FOR THEIR OWN INFRASTRUCTURE

If a data center requires:

• Roads
• Water lines
• Sewer systems
• Electrical infrastructure
• Transmission lines
• Substations
• Emergency services
• Additional public safety resources

THE DATA CENTER PAYS THE INCREMENTAL COST.

No more privatizing the profits while taxpayers absorb the costs.

🔊 NOISE, AIR AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS MATTER

There should be strict, measurable limits.

24/7 monitoring.

Public reporting.

And if they violate the rules, there should be consequences severe enough that BREAKING THE RULES IS NEVER CHEAPER THAN FOLLOWING THEM.

🚨 PENALTIES MUST HAVE TEETH.

Not a slap on the wrist.
Not a cost of doing business.
Not a negotiated settlement behind closed doors.

Violations should result in:

MASSIVE FINES.

LOSS OF TAX INCENTIVES.

REPAYMENT OF COMMUNITY DAMAGES.

SUSPENSION OF OPERATIONS FOR SERIOUS VIOLATIONS.

And for repeated or intentional violations, the company should be subject to LOSS OF ITS OPERATING PERMIT.

🚫 NO PAY-TO-PLAY POLITICS.

A data center should NOT be able to wait for a new mayor, city council, county commissioner or other local administration and then simply buy its way into weaker rules.

The rules should be established by law and apply consistently.

Local governments should NOT be allowed to waive critical protections because of political contributions, campaign support, personal relationships or financial incentives.

No sweetheart deals.

No backroom amendments.

No special exemptions for politically connected companies.

No “grandfathering” a facility into weaker standards simply because a new administration takes office.

THE RULES SHOULD NOT CHANGE BECAUSE THE POLITICAL PEOPLE CHANGE.

If a company agrees to the rules when it builds the facility, those obligations should follow the property and the operating permit.

The standards should be:

CLEAR.
PUBLIC.
ENFORCEABLE.
CONSISTENT.

🇺🇸 BUILD THE DATA CENTERS.

Build the AI infrastructure.

Keep America technologically competitive.

Create American jobs.

Strengthen our national security.

But DON’T MAKE AMERICANS PAY THE PRICE.

The deal should be simple:

You want to build here?

Then protect our privacy.

Pay your full costs.

Recycle your water.

Don’t burden our power grid.

Don’t pollute our communities.

Follow the rules.

And don’t buy politicians to change the rules.

AMERICA SHOULD WELCOME INNOVATION WITHOUT SURRENDERING AMERICAN PRIVACY, RESOURCES OR COMMUNITIES.

BUILD IT.

BUT BUILD IT RIGHT.

🇺🇸
